newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares fall despite phosphate gains.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares fall despite phosphate gains.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell back Saturday in quiet trade despite a strong performance by Jordan Phosphate Mines, a leading exporter which reported a healthy rise in 1996 revenues last week.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.20 points to 153.81 points in turnover of just 321,000 dinars ($453,000).
Jordan Phosphate Mines accounted for over 40 percent of Saturday's trade, rising 0.07 dinars to 3.40 dinars. But it was one of only five shares to rise compared to 16 which fell.
Blue-chip Arab Bank was unchanged after shares worth 56,000 shares changed hands and no other company attracted turnover of more than 16,000 dinars.
"The preliminary results were good for 1996 and profits are expected to be around 20 million dinars," one broker said. "That would give the firm a P/E ratio of just six."
Jordan Petroleum Refinery, which had risen steadily since Jordan's agreement last week for cheap Iraqi oil through 1997, fell 0.03 dinars to 9.95 dinars in trade worth nearly 12,000 dinars.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.17 percent to 81.92 points.
